claim: Capacity reservations give dedicated serverless processing capacity for Athena queries. The capacity is serverless and fully managed by Athena, and no changes to your SQL queries are required.
question: What do Athena capacity reservations provide?

values.display: dedicated serverless processing capacity
no changes to your SQL queries are required

evidence.quote: You can use capacity reservations to get dedicated serverless processing capacity for the queries you run in Athena.
Capacity is serverless and fully-managed by Athena and held for you as long as you need it. Setup is easy and no changes to your SQL queries are required.

claim: To get processing capacity you create a capacity reservation, specify the number of Data Processing Units (DPUs) you need, and assign one or more workgroups to the reservation.
question: How do you set up Athena capacity reservations?

values.display: specify the number of Data Processing Units (DPUs)
assign one or more workgroups to the reservation

evidence.quote: To get processing capacity for your queries, you create a capacity reservation, specify the number of Data Processing Units (DPUs) that you require, and assign one or more workgroups to the reservation.

claim: Queries in workgroups assigned to a capacity reservation run on your reserved capacity and do not count towards your DDL and DML query quota, which gives them priority.
question: Do queries on a capacity reservation count toward the Athena DML and DDL query quota?

values.display: do not count towards your DDL and DML query quota
give priority to these queries

qualifiers.scope: workgroups assigned to a capacity reservation

evidence.quote: Assigning workgroups to capacity reservations lets you give priority to these queries because they run on your reserved capacity and do not count towards your DDL and DML query quota.

claim: To make sure an important workload has capacity, assign its workgroup to a capacity reservation. Only queries from the assigned workgroup use the reservation's capacity.
question: How do you isolate critical Athena queries from other workloads?

values.display: assign its workgroup to the reservation
Only queries from the assigned workgroup use the processing capacity

evidence.quote: Isolate important queries – To ensure that an important workload has the capacity it needs when you need it, create a capacity reservation and assign its workgroup to the reservation. Only queries from the assigned workgroup use the processing capacity from your reservation.

claim: Multiple workloads can share capacity from one reservation, which gives a predictable cost and controls their concurrency.
question: Why share one Athena capacity reservation across workgroups?

values.display: Multiple workloads can share capacity from one reservation
achieve a predictable cost for these workloads

evidence.quote: Share capacity across similar workloads – Multiple workloads can share capacity from one reservation. This allows you to achieve a predictable cost for these workloads and control their concurrency.

claim: A DPU represents the serverless compute and memory resources Athena uses to process data. One DPU typically provides 4 vCPUs and 16 GB of memory, and more DPUs allow more concurrent queries.
question: What is an Athena DPU?

values.display: One DPU typically provides 4 vCPUs and 16 GB of memory
influences the number of queries that you can run concurrently

evidence.quote: One DPU typically provides 4 vCPUs and 16 GB of memory. The number of DPUs that you hold influences the number of queries that you can run concurrently.

claim: If reserved capacity is busy, newly submitted queries are queued until capacity is available, for up to 10 hours.
question: What happens to queries when an Athena capacity reservation is fully busy?

values.display: newly submitted queries are queued until capacity is available
maximum allowed time in queue is 10 hours

evidence.quote: If your capacity is busy serving other queries, newly submitted queries are queued until capacity is available. The maximum allowed time in queue is 10 hours.

claim: You can use capacity reservations and per-query billing based on data scanned at the same time in one account, but a workgroup can be assigned to only one capacity reservation at a time.
question: Can an account use both on-demand and reserved Athena capacity, and how many reservations can a workgroup use?

values.display: capacity reservations and per-query billing, based on data scanned, at the same time
assigned to one capacity reservation at a time

evidence.quote: You can use capacity reservations and per-query billing, based on data scanned, at the same time in the same account.
A workgroup can be assigned to one capacity reservation at a time.

claim: Capacity reservations do not support workgroups that are configured to use Apache Spark.
question: Can Athena Spark workgroups use capacity reservations?

values.display: Workgroups configured to use Apache Spark are not supported
capacity reservations

evidence.quote: Workgroups configured to use Apache Spark are not supported.

claim: Athena can run read, time travel, write and DDL queries on Apache Iceberg tables. Iceberg supports record-level insert, update, delete and time travel queries.
question: What operations does Athena support on Apache Iceberg tables?

values.display: read, time travel, write, and DDL queries
record-level insert, update, delete, and time travel queries

evidence.quote: You can use Athena to perform read, time travel, write, and DDL queries on Apache Iceberg tables.

Apache Iceberg is an open table format for very large analytic datasets. Iceberg manages large collections of files as tables, and it supports modern analytical data lake operations such as record-level insert, update, delete, and time travel queries.

claim: The Iceberg specification allows seamless table evolution such as schema and partition evolution, and Iceberg helps guarantee data correctness under concurrent write scenarios.
question: What does Iceberg add for data lake tables on S3?

values.display: seamless table evolution such as schema and partition evolution
guarantee data correctness under concurrent write scenarios

evidence.quote: The Iceberg specification allows seamless table evolution such as schema and partition evolution and is designed for optimized usage on Amazon S3. Iceberg also helps guarantee data correctness under concurrent write scenarios.

claim: Athena supports only AWS Glue optimistic locking for Iceberg tables. Modifying an Iceberg table with Athena under any other lock implementation can cause data loss and break transactions.
question: Which locking does Athena support for Iceberg tables?

values.display: Athena supports AWS Glue optimistic locking only
potential data loss and break transactions

evidence.quote: Table locking support by AWS Glue only – Unlike the open source Glue catalog implementation, which supports plug-in custom locking, Athena supports AWS Glue optimistic locking only. Using Athena to modify an Iceberg table with any other lock implementation will cause potential data loss and break transactions.

claim: Athena creates and operates only on Iceberg v2 tables.
question: Which Iceberg table format version does Athena use?

values.display: Athena only creates and operates on Iceberg v2 tables
Iceberg v2 tables

evidence.quote: Iceberg v2 tables – Athena only creates and operates on Iceberg v2 tables.

claim: Lake Formation can manage read access for transactional table formats such as Iceberg, Hudi and Delta Lake, but cannot manage permissions for operations like VACUUM, MERGE, UPDATE or OPTIMIZE on them.
question: Can Lake Formation control MERGE, UPDATE and VACUUM on Iceberg tables used with Athena?

values.display: manage read access permissions for TransactionTable Formats
VACUUM, MERGE, UPDATE or OPTIMIZE

qualifiers.scope: Iceberg, Hudi and Delta Lake tables used with Athena

evidence.quote: TTF management commands not supported in AWS Lake Formation – Although you can use Lake Formation to manage read access permissions for TransactionTable Formats (TTFs) like Apache Iceberg, Apache Hudi, and Linux Foundation Delta Lake, you cannot use Lake Formation to manage permissions for operations like VACUUM, MERGE, UPDATE or OPTIMIZE with these table formats.

claim: Athena ACID transactions let multiple users concurrently and reliably add and delete S3 objects atomically while isolating existing queries with read consistency, and they add single-table insert, delete, update and time travel to Athena DML.
question: What do Athena ACID transactions provide?

values.display: concurrently and reliably add and delete Amazon S3 objects in an atomic manner
single-table support for insert, delete, update, and time travel operations

evidence.quote: ACID transactions enable multiple users to concurrently and reliably add and delete Amazon S3 objects in an atomic manner, while isolating any existing queries by maintaining read consistency for queries against the data lake. Athena ACID transactions add single-table support for insert, delete, update, and time travel operations to the Athena SQL data manipulation language (DML).

claim: Athena transactions manage locking and coordination automatically, with no custom record locking solution needed. A SQL DELETE can respond to a data erasure request, and time travel queries can recover recently deleted data.
question: How can Athena handle a data erasure request on S3 data?

values.display: do not require a custom record locking solution
respond to a data erasure request, you can perform a SQL DELETE operation

evidence.quote: Athena transactions automatically manage locking semantics and coordination and do not require a custom record locking solution.
For example, to respond to a data erasure request, you can perform a SQL DELETE operation.
To recover data that was recently deleted, you can issue time travel queries using a SELECT statement.

claim: Because Athena ACID transactions are built on shared table formats, they are compatible with other engines such as Amazon EMR and Apache Spark that support the same formats.
question: Can EMR and Spark read tables that use Athena ACID transactions?

values.display: built on shared table formats
compatible with other services and engines such as Amazon EMR

qualifiers.condition: the other engine supports the shared table formats

evidence.quote: Because they are built on shared table formats, Athena ACID transactions are compatible with other services and engines such as Amazon EMR and Apache Spark that also support shared table formats.

claim: Apache Spark on Athena lets you run analytics interactively without planning for, configuring or managing resources. It is serverless with automatic, on-demand scaling and instant-on compute.
question: What is Apache Spark on Amazon Athena?

values.display: without the need to plan for, configure, or manage resources
automatic, on-demand scaling that delivers instant-on compute

evidence.quote: Amazon Athena makes it easy to interactively run data analytics and exploration using Apache Spark without the need to plan for, configure, or manage resources.
Apache Spark on Amazon Athena is serverless and provides automatic, on-demand scaling that delivers instant-on compute to meet changing data volumes and processing requirements.

claim: Athena for Apache Spark automatically determines the compute and memory a job needs and scales them continuously up to the maximums you specify, which reduces cost without affecting speed.
question: How does Athena for Apache Spark scale?

values.display: continuously scales those resources accordingly up to the maximums that you specify
reduces cost without affecting speed

evidence.quote: Dynamic scaling – Amazon Athena automatically determines the compute and memory resources needed to run a job and continuously scales those resources accordingly up to the maximums that you specify. This dynamic scaling reduces cost without affecting speed.

claim: Athena's SQL considerations list UPDATE statements and DELETE FROM as unsupported statements, and state that MERGE is supported only for transactional table formats.
question: Which row-level statements does Athena list as unsupported for SQL queries?

values.display: UPDATE statements are not supported
supported only for transactional table formats

qualifiers.scope: Athena SQL queries; MERGE needs transactional table formats such as Iceberg

evidence.quote: UPDATE statements are not supported.
DELETE FROM is not supported.
The MERGE statement is supported only for transactional table formats.

claim: Athena does not support stored procedures, and does not support Trino or Presto connectors; use Athena Federated Query to connect data sources.
question: Does Athena support stored procedures or Trino connectors?

values.display: Stored procedures are not supported
Use Amazon Athena Federated Query to connect data sources

evidence.quote: Stored procedures – Stored procedures are not supported.
Trino and Presto connectors – Neither Trino nor Presto connectors are supported. Use Amazon Athena Federated Query to connect data sources.

claim: Athena can time out on tables with many thousands of partitions that are not of type string. With type string it prunes partitions at the metastore level; with other types it prunes on the server side, which is slower.
question: Why can Athena time out on tables with many partitions, and what is the fix?

values.display: set your partition type to string
Athena prunes partitions at the metastore level

qualifiers.scope: tables with many thousands of partitions

evidence.quote: Athena may time out when querying a table that has many thousands of partitions. This can happen when the table has many partitions that are not of type string. When you use type string, Athena prunes partitions at the metastore level. However, when you use other data types, Athena prunes partitions on the server side.

claim: Athena treats source files that start with an underscore or a dot as hidden. To work around this, rename the files.
question: Why does Athena skip some files in an S3 location?

values.display: source files that start with an underscore
rename the files

evidence.quote: Athena treats source files that start with an underscore (_) or a dot (.) as hidden. To work around this limitation, rename the files.
